purpose: Independent simulated beginner observation using the fixed report questions.
persona: Simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in a short ambient soundtrack sketch.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Completed the composition, naming, save, and both exports with mouse controls. The empty-space MIDI hint and on-screen naming keyboard helped. Exact durations took many stepper clicks.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The restrained dark theme, teal waveforms, MIDI note previews, and yellow playhead looked clean and readable. The piano roll looked comparatively dense.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most edits and instrument assignment responded promptly, and duplication sped up the arrangement. WAV export displayed elapsed progress and completed within the observed session. Screenshot/tool time is not a performance benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Most labels were clear. Duplicate in the context menu acted immediately, while the toolbar only selected a tool; clicking it twice did not add clips. Duration is entered in beats, so the seconds readout was needed to reach 30 seconds.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The tested workflow provided audio, MIDI drawing, VST assignment, stretching, trimming, volume, naming, project saving, and WAV/MIDI export. This session used only one simple installed VST and did not establish broader plugin or sound-design capabilities.

findings.observation: File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Clicking its keys entered mist and Apply name changed the visible project title.
The empty arranger said Double-click for MIDI. Double-clicking it opened the Device library; Assign instrument created a MIDI clip and displayed Rill Lab Sine on the track.
Pencil drags created visible C4, E4, and G4 notes. The clip properties offered Stretch and an exact elapsed-time readout, enabling a 7.5-second sustained chord clip.
Clicking the duration field selected its text but did not expose an on-screen numeric keypad. I used repeated plus/minus clicks to set exact beat durations.
Context-menu Duplicate immediately added a clip. Clicking the toolbar Duplicate twice only highlighted the tool; the total stayed 15 seconds until I clicked a clip, which then made it 22.5 seconds.

Using the Duplicate tool on clips made four MIDI clips. Three further audio copies and trimming the final audio clip to 8 beats brought the visible project duration to 0:30.000. The audio track was lowered to -27.6 dB.
Play became Pause, the playhead advanced from the start, the transport changed to 003.04.65, and both track meters showed activity. Stop returned playback to the beginning.
The native save dialogs automatically proposed mist.rill, mist.wav, and mist.mid in the session-4 directory. Saving the project closed the dialog and removed the dot beside the title.
WAV export showed Arrangement 0:30; I unchecked Include effect tails. It displayed progress, then Exported · mist.wav. MIDI export also displayed Exported · mist.mid.

The first screenshot after opening native save and MIDI export dialogs showed a black rectangle; a later screenshot showed the completed dialog. This was brief and did not block completion in the laboratory desktop.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: named and saved a 30-second arrangement and saw success notices for WAV and MIDI exports; output contents await independent verification.
outcome.composition: Four consecutive 7.5-second MIDI clips containing sustained C4/E4/G4 notes, with the startup Circuit rhythm audio copied across the arrangement and its final copy trimmed to end at 30 seconds. Audio track volume was reduced to -27.6 dB for a quiet rhythmic bed under the chord sketch.
outcome.playback_observed: Visible playhead motion, changing transport position, and activity on both audio and instrument track meters; no playback failure observed. Audio was not auditioned.

limitations: No output file contents were inspected and no audio capture was auditioned. Audible balance, quality, and final file duration/PCM remain for independent coordinator verification.
Only the installed laboratory Rill Lab Sine VST3 was tested; results do not establish compatibility with other plugins.
The environment uses software graphics and a timer-paced virtual audio sink. Observed elapsed time includes tool, screenshot, and reporting overhead and is not a hardware performance benchmark.
The composition is a simple ambient-oriented chord sketch with a quiet rhythmic bed; its musical sound was not verified by listening.
